company.name: Pennine Scholar Transport Ltd
company.description: Dedicated home-to-school and campus transport operator running contracted morning and afternoon school runs, SEN (special educational needs) passenger transport, and university inter-campus and late-night safe shuttle services across West Yorkshire and Greater Manchester. PSV operator (O) licence holder with operating centres in Leeds and Manchester. Holds local-authority home-to-school framework contracts, operates a fully DBS-checked and MiDAS-accredited driver and passenger-assistant workforce, and provides live GPS parent-notification and pupil boarding/alighting tracking on every vehicle.

metadata.generatedNote: Operating data for a typical term-time week (2026-06-22 to 2026-06-28) at a small UK home-to-school and campus transport operator. Reflects DVSA MOT (PSV annual test), PSV operator (O) licence and Traffic Commissioner undertakings, GB domestic and EU/GB drivers' hours under the smart tachograph regime, DVLA category D/D1 licensing, Driver CPC, enhanced DBS with barred-list checks, MiDAS minibus driver and passenger-assistant accreditation, PSVAR 2000 accessibility and safeguarding under Keeping Children Safe in Education. Focus areas are pupil boarding and alighting headcounts, route bell-times and special-needs requirements, pre- and post-trip safety inspections, driver licensing and background checks, and live GPS parent notification on boarding and alighting.

notes.author: Rashid Khan (DRV-203, PA dual-role)
notes.body: No-handover situation at the Wythenshawe drop this afternoon. The named carer was not at the door when we arrived and was not answering the phone. I followed the procedure: I kept the pupil secured and calm on board, called the duty controller, and we worked through the emergency contacts. A neighbour who is listed as an emergency contact came out and the parent confirmed by phone that this was acceptable, so the neighbour collected the pupil and signed. I have logged the time, the calls made, and the outcome for the local authority.

notes.author: Workshop (Colin Whitaker)
notes.body: Coach 209 declared VOR after the daily check found the front nearside brake binding with excessive heat at the hub. Stripped the caliper and found it seized; replacement on order from the local distributor for Friday. Spare relief vehicle reallocated to cover the Route 1 PM duty in the meantime. Pre-MOT prep for this vehicle deferred until the caliper is fitted.

notes.author: Operations (Diane Pickersgill liaison)
notes.body: Confirmed with Brookside SEN Academy that all three wheelchair care plans are current and that the epilepsy emergency-medication protocol for the second pupil is held by the passenger assistant. The named-staff handover list at the academy has been updated for the term. Banksman is provided by the academy for the reverse onto the accessible bay.

notes.author: Operations (Helen Marsden liaison)
notes.body: Leeds City Council home-to-school framework review meeting held. Confirmed all drivers on the framework hold an enhanced DBS with a barred-list check and current MiDAS where minibuses are used. Pupil headcount procedure (at each pickup and at school, then at school and each drop on the return) was demonstrated and accepted. Parent-notify is enabled on the contracts that requested it.

notes.author: Compliance (Andrew Sutcliffe)
notes.body: Patricia's Driver CPC card expires on 30 July. Periodic training is booked for 10 July so she remains qualified. Reminder set to verify the new card is recorded before the autumn term. Her MiDAS PATS and barred-list DBS remain in date.

notes.author: Liam Connolly (DRV-205)
notes.body: Campus loop ran well today. Late-night safe shuttle from 20:00 with student ID scan on boarding worked smoothly; eight students on the final run, all alighted safely at Bodington Fields and I confirmed the saloon was empty before heading back. RTPI to the campus app stayed accurate within a minute all day.

notes.author: Liam Connolly (DRV-205)
notes.body: EV shuttle started the day at 96% and held range well on the morning loop. Mid-shift opportunity charge at the depot took it from 38% to 82% in about 40 minutes, plenty for the afternoon. Students keep commenting on how quiet it is at the stops. Regen braking noticeably helping on the Woodhouse Lane descent.

notes.author: Rashid Khan (DRV-203, PA dual-role)
notes.body: Recorded here for the route file: the no-handover escalation at this drop was resolved with a listed emergency contact collecting the pupil after the parent confirmed by phone. Full timeline captured in the route note and reported to the local authority travel team the same evening.

The individual care plan and the route risk assessment must be signed off by the academy travel lead before the pupil travels.
